annotations.text:
DECISION: Almanac structure, the app's own font, and now TWELVE palettes ranging the spectrum — whites, greys, and tinted papers — each with a designed light AND dark variant, plus Light / Dark / System theme control (per-user, synced).

Index card top-left; Appearance settings beside it; full dashboard renders below — three light rows, then three dark rows, in the same spectrum order.

Room colors: three shared ramps — Vivid (Gallery), Mono (Ink, Graphite), Field (everything else — accent + five muted co-colors drawn from a validated pool; the accent's hue-neighbor is dropped per palette). Base pools pass the color-blind validator in both modes; each palette's final six-color ramp gets a per-palette validation pass during implementation.

Earlier direction explorations live on the second page (pages menu in the toolbar).

Next: the spec (homechronicle-ui-spec.md) goes into GSD for milestone planning.

Dark is a palette, not a filter

Each world's dark mode re-derives every token: surfaces get a hue-tinted near-black (green-black for Porcelain, blue-black for Dusk, warm black for Ink, neutral for Gallery), text goes to toned off-whites, and all six room colors are re-stepped to a uniform lightness so they read as the same rooms without glowing.

Every colored room set passes the color-blind separation validator in both modes; room identity is never color-alone (name labels everywhere).

Maps onto the existing theme machinery: html.theme-dark class + a new data-palette attribute replacing data-accent, System via prefers-color-scheme.

B · CONSOLE — instrument panel

Built for the self-hoster: dark by default, JetBrains Mono, one phosphor-amber accent, hard corners, hairline panels, a status bar with listener/DB/device health, keyboard hints (1–5, j/k, /). The Timeline is a dense log table with a query bar and a RAW / EPISODES switch.

Why: honest about what the product is (a log). Highest information density; stale devices and faults get first-class real estate.
Tradeoff: least friendly to a non-technical household member; light theme is secondary and will feel like 'a terminal in daylight'.

C · HEARTH — domestic / spatial

The house is the organizing idea. Bricolage Grotesque display + Public Sans, warm paper, clay/olive/ochre/night palette. The dashboard opens with a sentence about the house, a room map sized by activity (replaces the room bar list), and a day arc for quiet hours. Timeline entries are written as small headlines on a thread, grouped into episodes.

Why: most distinctive at a glance and the most approachable for everyone in the home; the episode grouping the app already computes becomes the star.
Tradeoff: lowest data density; needs good copy generation for the headlines; room colors become a real design token set (7+ hues) that must pass contrast in both themes.

D · BLUEPRINT — technical drawing

The home as a set of drawings: cyanotype blue ground, drafting grid, white line-work, Saira Condensed caps + Space Mono numerals. Charts are 'sections' and 'elevations'; rooms are an outlined plan view with hatching; version info lives in a title block.

Why: instantly unforgettable, and the drawing metaphor fits an append-only record of a dwelling.
Tradeoff: the most committed bit — a light theme barely makes sense; long dense pages (Settings) need care so the conceit doesn't get exhausting.

E · SIGNAL — Swiss / international style

White, black, one red. Archivo Black numerals at poster scale, hard 1px column rules instead of cards, flat marks, numbered sections (01/02/03). No gradients, no shadows, no rounding anywhere.

Why: timeless rather than trendy; huge numbers make the daily glance effortless; easiest of the five to implement precisely with Tailwind tokens.
Tradeoff: closest cousin to A (both editorial-reductive) — sterile if the copywriting is lazy; dark mode is straightforward but the red must be re-tuned.

F · ALMANAC — the A×C blend

From A (Ledger): masthead nav, ruled sections, serif display numerals, mono data values, editorial restraint.
From C (Hearth): the greeting sentence as the page's lede, the room map sized by activity, the day-rhythm arc, headline-style timeline entries, and warm color.

Why: reader-first like A, but rooms and episodes carry color so the household can read it at a glance — the data stays the eye-candy, not decoration.
Tradeoff: two voices to keep in balance — the copy generation (headlines, lede) must be reliable, and the room palette becomes a maintained token set with a dark-mode variant.

A · LEDGER — editorial / print

A 'chronicle' is a record; this treats it like a well-set ledger or broadsheet. Newsreader serif for headings and big numbers, IBM Plex Sans body, Plex Mono for every value. No cards: hairline rules, a masthead nav, a 4-column ledger row, ink-only charts with one oxblood accent.

Why: the most un-app-like of the three; numbers become the visual identity. Ages well.
Tradeoff: dark mode must be designed as its own palette (warm ink on charcoal), not a flip; dense pages (Devices, Settings) need discipline to stay 'ruled' rather than 'table-y'.

NOW EXPANDED → to the right: the Devices page and the dark mode (warm charcoal + cream ink, lightened oxblood), so you can judge A beyond the dashboard.

The editable dashboard is KEPT

This board shows the same dashboard with Customize on. Nothing about the grid changes — only the skin:

• All 24 registered panels survive with their ids (12 core + 12 optional). The hidden-panel tray, drag handles, × remove, corner resize, lg/sm breakpoints and per-user saved layouts behave exactly as they do today.
• The Almanac 'sections' ARE panels: the ledger stat row is the existing `kpis` panel (already bare) restyled; the thirty-day chart is `trend`; by-hour is `hourly`; by-room is `rooms`.
• Three NEW panels join the registry: House Summary (the lede), Where things happen (room map), Today's rhythm (arc).
• In view mode panels show no header — each panel component supplies its own title, which is what makes the hairline editorial look possible without touching grid mechanics.
